official.deadline_note: 1 June and 1 November are the mobility-application deadlines published by the Central CEEPUS Office: 1 June for the following winter term and 1 November for the following summer term (freemover applications also fall on 1 July and 1 November). The separate 'Network Application Round 2027/28' that closes 30 November 2026 (signed letters by 15 December 2026) is for institutions and faculty coordinators, not students, and each National CEEPUS Office and network may run its own internal cut-offs earlier.
official.application_cycle: Annual cycle - student and freemover mobility applications for the following summer term close 1 November 2026; network application round 2027/28 opened 21 September 2026
official.status_note: The Central CEEPUS Office announced on 21 September 2026 that the 'Network Application Round 2027/28' is enabled with a deadline of 30 November 2026, 23:59 CET and an extended deadline for signed documents (letters) of 15 December 2026, 23:59 CET; mobility applications are submitted through the 'My CEEPUS' online tool.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Within a network incoming students are exempted from paying tuition fees (study.gov.pl); each host country pays its incoming students and teachers directly, there is no central transfer of funds.
benefits: Exemption from tuition fees at the host institution for incoming students within a network

A monthly grant paid by the host country's National CEEPUS Office; the individual monthly grant rate depends on the host country and the grants are comprehensive grants linked to the local cost of living

Published 2026/2027 student monthly rates: Albania 40,000 LEK; Austria EUR 1,300; Bosnia and Herzegovina EUR 360; Bulgaria EUR 127 (Bachelor/Master); Croatia EUR 240 plus free dormitory accommodation and a subsidised-meal x-card; Czech Republic 14,000 CZK; Hungary 190,000 HUF; Kosovo EUR 250 (public universities); Montenegro EUR 100; North Macedonia EUR 175; Moldova 5,620 LEI; Poland 2,500 PLN; Romania EUR 120; Serbia 40,000 RSD; Slovakia EUR 620; Slovenia EUR 400
Some CEEPUS countries pay an extra allowance or a travel reimbursement in addition to the monthly rate - always ask the National CEEPUS Office of both the host and the home country
Each country has to pledge at least 100 scholarship months per academic year
eligibility: Citizenship of a CEEPUS member state - Albania, Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, the Czech Republic, Hungary, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Poland, Romania, Serbia, the Slovak Republic and Slovenia; the universities of Prishtina, Prizren and Peja also participate
Enrolled at, or employed by, a university eligible under CEEPUS (each country nominates its list of eligible universities annually)
Students must have successfully completed two semesters of a regular course of studies (one completed semester is enough for intensive courses)
Grants for studying in one's own home country are not permitted; exchange stays based on nationality are only possible for teachers in most CEEPUS countries
Applicants without CEEPUS citizenship may qualify with an 'equal status document'; teachers must be employed full-time by a university in a CEEPUS network or umbrella network
Ukrainian students and teachers of Ukrainian higher education institutions are eligible subject to availability of unused scholarship funds in the respective country
requirements: Home institution must participate in a funded CEEPUS network (found via the 'Find a network' database) or the applicant applies as a freemover
Contact the network coordinator, or the network partner at the home university, before applying to confirm a mobility is possible for the desired guest university
Students apply online through the 'My CEEPUS' application tool after registering an account
Teachers must teach or supervise 6 hours for each work week (5 days) spent in the host country and must enter the exact titles and hours in the mobility application before the grant is awarded
CEEPUS grants are limited to 12 months for each BA and MA cycle; there is no restriction for PhD students; each teacher may apply for a maximum of 10 scholarship stays per academic year
No double grants are allowed - an applicant may not receive another grant simultaneously in the host country
documents: Applicants who are citizens of a CEEPUS member state do not have to upload documents for a network mobility
Freemover students: a freemover letter of acceptance from the host institution plus two freemover letters of recommendation from the home institution (templates in the Downloads section)
Freemover teachers: one freemover letter of acceptance - teacher from the host institution
Non-CEEPUS citizens: proof of full-time student status and an 'equal status document' (confirmation of enrolment or employment)
Ukrainian applicants: proof of enrolment or employment at a Ukrainian higher education institution
After the stay: a Mobility Report completed online and a printed, signed and stamped Letter of Confirmation uploaded again - the QR code changes if the letter is edited after printing
selection_criteria: No published central selection criteria for student mobility; the application is processed and forwarded and the National CEEPUS Office of the guest country awards the grant
Networks are formally correct applications evaluated by CEEPUS experts and selected on overall ranking; the available quota is set by the International Commission each year in February
Networks not ranked high enough for full funding may receive 'umbrella' status, and unused scholarship months can later be assigned to them by a National CEEPUS Office
coverage: Tuition fee exemption for incoming students within a network
Monthly grant sized to the living costs of the host country, covering food, accommodation and, in several countries, basic health insurance and local transport

Country-specific extras published with the rates: Croatia arranges and pays dormitory accommodation and a canteen x-card; Slovenia arranges dormitory accommodation (EUR 100-200 per month), basic medical insurance (EUR 254.19 per month), food coupons and public transport subsidy; Slovakia and Poland include basic medical insurance where needed; Moldova pays a separate accommodation allowance
Travel reimbursement is not guaranteed: it depends on the home country of the university and must be requested from the National CEEPUS Office of the home country
application_method: Use the 'Find a network' database to check whether the home institution takes part in a funded CEEPUS network
Get in contact with the network coordinator, or with the National CEEPUS Office for freemover applications
Register or log in to 'My CEEPUS' and complete the online Mobility Application form
The National CEEPUS Office of the guest country awards the grant, usually within two weeks to a month; the status is shown in the CEEPUS account
official.application_route: Apply online through the 'My CEEPUS' tool, entering through a funded CEEPUS network at the home institution (or as a freemover via the National CEEPUS Office of the target country); the host country's National CEEPUS Office ultimately awards the grant.
official.study_mode: Full-time (students must hold full-time student status; teachers must be employed full-time by a CEEPUS university)
official.citizenship_residency: Must be a citizen of a CEEPUS member state (15 member states; the universities of Prishtina, Prizren and Peja also participate). Holders of another citizenship may apply with an 'equal status document'; in some CEEPUS countries this is restricted to EU/EEA citizens only.
official.international_eligibility: Yes for nationals of the 15 CEEPUS member states; non-CEEPUS citizens enrolled or employed at a CEEPUS university may be eligible under national rules, and Ukrainian higher education institutions were opened to the programme subject to available funds
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Mobilities take place within a thematic CEEPUS network of eligible universities, so the field is effectively restricted to what the funded networks cover; freemovers may choose any eligible institution of any CEEPUS country
official.duration: Student semester exchanges: minimum 3 months and maximum 10 months; short-term student stays under 3 months are limited to thesis or dissertation work and intensive short programmes; excursions from 3 days; university staff 2-5 working days
official.description: CEEPUS, the Central European Exchange Program for University Studies, is a multilateral exchange programme of the extended Danube region run through subject-specific networks of eligible universities in 15 member states, with the universities of Prishtina, Prizren and Peja also participating. Incoming students are exempted from tuition fees and receive a monthly grant from the host country, sized according to local living costs, for exchanges of 3 to 10 months. Each country pays its own incoming students and teachers directly through its National CEEPUS Office.
official.region: Central and Eastern Europe (Albania, Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic, Hungary, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, plus Kosovo universities)
official.program_type: Multilateral university exchange programme (network mobility and freemover grants for students, teachers, university staff and network meetings)

not_confirmed: funding_amount, funding_currency and funding_period: no single programme-wide figure exists - the official site publishes a separate monthly rate per host country and per applicant category, so the published 2026/2027 rates are quoted verbatim in benefits and coverage instead of being reduced to one number
travel_coverage: officially described as depending on the home country of the university, so it cannot be confirmed programme-wide
english_requirement: no English language requirement is published by CEEPUS or on the study.gov.pl page
research_requirement: no research proposal requirement is published for CEEPUS student mobility
verification.notes: Amounts, deadlines, eligibility rules and application steps were taken from the Central CEEPUS Office pages (how / apply / contact / about) including the per-country 2026/2027 scholarship-rate tables on the National CEEPUS Office contact page, and cross-checked against the study.gov.pl programme page for tuition exemption, duration and country list.

applicant_utility.summary: CEEPUS is not a central scholarship you apply for directly - it is funded by the host country, so the money, the paperwork and the deadlines all flow through your home institution's CEEPUS network and the National CEEPUS Office of the country you want to visit. Check the 'Find a network' database first: if your institute is not in a funded network you must apply as a freemover, which needs a host acceptance letter and two recommendation letters before you can even open the form. Then email the network coordinator early, because the slot has to exist in the network's traffic sheet before your application means anything, and submit through 'My CEEPUS' well before 1 November (summer term) or 1 June (winter term) - the award is made by the host country's office and takes two weeks to a month.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Students and teachers at a university that already sits inside a funded CEEPUS network in their field, who want a 3-10 month tuition-free exchange in Central or Eastern Europe and can live on a modest local monthly stipend.
application_readiness_checklist: Search the 'Find a network' database for your home institution and note the network coordinator's name and email
Email the coordinator (or your National CEEPUS Office for freemover route) to ask whether a mobility to your target university is possible this cycle and get the acceptance agreed in writing first
Confirm you have completed at least two semesters of a regular course of studies, or one semester for an intensive course
Register an account in 'My CEEPUS' before the deadline and complete the online Mobility Application form, including exact teaching or supervision titles and hours if you are teaching
Prepare freemover documents in advance - host letter of acceptance plus two letters of recommendation on the official templates from the Downloads section
Check your home and host National CEEPUS Office pages for the actual monthly rate, accommodation arrangements and whether a travel refund exists, then budget the difference
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a university that is not a partner in a funded network or umbrella network for the intended term
Missing that the host country's own National CEEPUS Office has run out of scholarship months, or that freemover grants are only available for one semester in some countries
Submitting after the internal network cut-off even though the central deadline looks far away
Holding a second grant in the host country, which is explicitly barred and can disqualify an otherwise eligible application
Teachers failing to guarantee the required 6 teaching or supervision hours per work week, or entering the activity after the award
Applying for a stay in the country of your own nationality as a student, which is not permitted
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Travel to and from the host country unless the home country's National CEEPUS Office grants a refund, plus anything above the monthly rate - in countries such as Croatia from 2026/2027 teachers no longer receive dormitory accommodation, and in Slovenia or North Macedonia accommodation arrangements differ by category. Visa, insurance beyond the basic cover some countries include, registration and personal living costs beyond the local-rate stipend are also on the applicant.
document_audit: The tempting trap is uploading nothing: citizens of CEEPUS states file no documents for a network mobility, but freemovers must add a host acceptance letter and two recommendations on the exact templates
Non-CEEPUS citizens need proof of full-time status plus an equal-status document, and some countries accept only EU/EEA citizens for that route
The post-stay Letter of Confirmation must be printed, signed, stamped and re-uploaded - if it is edited online after printing the QR code changes and the upload is blocked
Dual citizens must pick one citizenship at the first application and use the same one for every later CEEPUS application
alerts: The 30 November 2026 deadline dominating the news page is the network application round for institutions, not the student scholarship call - students should watch 1 November 2026 for summer-term mobilities
Not every country accepts freemovers for both semesters, and Slovenia does not accept freemover teacher mobilities at all
Virtual mobility is only offered in Croatia, the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland, and hybrid or virtual awards are paid at a reduced share of the rate
Grants are capped at 12 months per BA and MA cycle, so a long CEEPUS history can consume the allowance before graduation
If the home university waives tuition, national law may treat that as a grant and block a second CEEPUS grant - check with the home National CEEPUS Office before applying
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Confirm a network or freemover route with the coordinator or National CEEPUS Office, complete the online Mobility Application in 'My CEEPUS', and wait for the guest country's National CEEPUS Office to award the grant (typically two weeks to a month), then arrange the stay with the host office.
